{{Quote|We were looking for Morodins. In the process we stumbled on the fact that they're more than just simple animals. They're fully sentient beings, aren't they, Gamgalon?|Talon Karrde realizes that the Morodins are more than what they appear to be|<ref name="FC" />}}
'''Morodins''' were a [[Species/Legends|species]] of large, [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Diet/Legends|herbivores]]. Often mistaken for massive herd animals, the Morodins had long, slender bodies that could grow up to twenty [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in length. They possessed six [[Limb/Legends|legs]] and two forearms, as well as a wide spoon-shaped [[Nose/Legends|snout]]. The most distinctive feature of the Morodins was their ability to secrete a nutrient slime trail that promoted growth and [[Mutant|mutation]] in [[Plant/Legends|plant]] life that it covered. The composition of the secretion varied with the Morodin's diet, and they were always experimenting with new combinations by eating plants, exuding the secretion to create a new, more nutritious, strain of flora which then entered their food chain.

Originally from a [[Morodin homeworld|homeworld]] that struggled to feed its growing population, the Morodins established a colony on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Varonat/Legends|Varonat]] to grow food. The Morodins turned part of Varonat into a vast [[Great Jungle|jungle]] and transported their bounty to the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] aboard [[organic space vessel]]s. However, an [[Unidentified ecological disaster|ecological disaster]] on their homeworld prevented the Morodins from growing their [[Starship/Legends|ships]], and contact with the homeworld was lost. The Morodins on Varonat continued to thrive. Eventually, [[Human/Legends|Human]] colonists reached Varonat and saw the Morodins as wild beasts intent on destroying their [[Farm/Legends|plantings]] when, in reality, the Morodins were trying to help the Humans to grow their food. During the early [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], a group of [[Krish (species)/Legends|Krish]] began planting in the jungle and actively allowing the Morodins to [[Fertilizer/Legends|fertilize]] the crop. At the same time, a [[Gamgalon's Morodin-hunting safari|safari]] had been established by the same group of Krish that [[Death/Legends|killed]] several Morodins a year as part of a big-game [[Hunting/Legends|hunt]].

==Biology and appearance==
[[File:Morodin-munching.jpg|thumb|left|A Morodin]]
{{Quote|How can the Morodins get through these trees? I thought they were big.''"<br />"''Morodins are long but slender. They can move easily about the jungle.|Quelev Tapper and Gamgalon's employee [[Falmal]] discuss the Morodins|<ref name="FC" />}}
Morodins were huge, [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]], [[Diet/Legends|herbivorous]],<ref name="FC" /> [[Mammal/Legends|mammalian]]<ref name="AE" /> [[Reptile/Legends|lizard]]&ndash;[[Gastropod/Legends|slugs]] that grew to between ten to twenty [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in length, but usually averaged about fifteen meters. Long and slender, the Morodins had no trouble navigating dense jungle [[Plant/Legends|foliage]]. Members of the species possessed six stubby [[Limb/Legends|legs]] with three-toed feet, and two short forearms that terminated in [[Claw/Legends|clawed]], three fingered hands. A long neck, which included prominent bulges where it connected to the lower jaw, supported a head with a spoon-billed [[Nose/Legends|snout]] full of flat [[Tooth/Legends|teeth]], and an [[Eye/Legends|eye]] on either side of a ridged cranium. [[Color/Legends|Yellow]] skin covered the Morodin body, with darker-colored mottling running down the back; a small tail protruded from the rear of the body. Morodins were generally peaceful and docile, even when confronted with a clear threat, and they moved relatively slowly. The Morodin produced a distinctive [[Morodin (language)|growl]], which they used for communication.<ref name="FC" />

Morodins exuded a nutrient [[Slime/Legends|slime]] trail that [[Fertilizer/Legends|fertilized]] soil and plant life, and was the basis for their unique form of biochemical agriculture. The slime was secreted from a gland located on the Morodins' underbelly. The nutrient content of the slime fluctuated with the Morodin's diet, and the resulting excretion encouraged growth and [[Mutant|mutation]] in plant life. By eating certain plants and then spreading the resultant slime over other vegetation, Morodins produced new species of flora. The new strains were more nutritious, and the Morodins added the resulting crop to their diet, in turn using it to create new secretions that produced yet more nutritious plants. The Morodins knew which combinations of food eaten and plants fertilized produced the best crop.<ref name="FC" />

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|Don't look at the Morodins. Look at the slime trails.''"<br />"''What about them?''"<br />"''Look at them. Tell me you see it, too.''"<br />"''I don't believe it.''"<br />"''I didn't either. Look&mdash;one of them's trying it.|Quelev Tapper and Talon Karrde realize the sentient nature of the Morodin after witnessing their maze&ndash;running|<ref name="FC" />}}
Only 50,000 Morodins were known to live on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Varonat/Legends|Varonat]], and they were organized into tribes. To completely fertilize an area, the Morodins had developed a form of maze&ndash;running; the elders of the tribe used their slime trails to create an elaborate and complex maze in a given area. The younger generation, as part of their education in the art of biochemical agriculture, then ran the maze to complete the fertilization. By using different slime patterns, the Morodins kept track of which combinations of nutrients were used to fertilize an area. At the height of their civilization, the Morodins had mastered [[Realspace/Legends|space travel]] and grew their own [[organic space vessel]]s, although they lost their ability to grow these [[Starship/Legends|starships]] when an [[Unidentified ecological disaster|ecological disaster]] occurred on their [[Morodin homeworld|homeworld]].<ref name="FC" />

==History==
{{Quote|Ever hear of Morodins?''"<br />"''I don't think so. Big game?''"<br />"''The biggest. Giant lizard-slug things, ten to twenty meters long. Make great wall or hallway trophies. They're not too fast or mean, either.|[[Fleck (Human)|Fleck]] discusses the traits of the Morodin with Talon Karrde|<ref name="FC" />}}
The Morodin civilization flourished on their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] before the formation of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. [[26,053 BBY|1,000]] [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before the Republic was founded, the Morodins established an agricultural colony on the planet Varonat in an effort to produce enough food to support their homeworld's growing population. Varonat was covered in immense plains, and the Morodins transported stores of food to the world to allow them, in conjunction with their own nutrient slimes, to convert the [[Grass/Legends|grasslands]] into edible plant life. The result produced the vast [[Great Jungle]] for which Varonat would become known thousands of years later.<ref name="FC" />

The colony on Varonat produced and harvested food, transporting it back to their homeworld aboard organic space vessels. Eventually, an ecological disaster on the Morodin homeworld stopped the Morodins from growing their organic starships. Cut off from their home planet, the colony on Varonat was left to its own devices. Over the [[Time/Legends|centuries]], the Morodins used their unique biochemical abilities to continually transform and modify Varonat's plant life to suit their needs, and gained an extensive knowledge of the native flora.<ref name="FC" />

In [[242 BBY/Legends|242 BBY]], [[Human/Legends|Human]] colonists from [[Salliche/Legends|Salliche]] led by [[Adarian Tropis]] settled on Varonat after [[Scout/Legends|scouting]] reports indicated rich, fertile soil in the Great Jungle. Settling [[Tropis-on-Varonat]], the colonists began [[Farm/Legends|planting crops]]. However, the fertility of the soil only lasted for a single season. The Morodins attempted to help the Humans by covering their crops with their nutrient slime. However, communication between the Morodins and the Humans proved to be impossible, and the Humans had no comprehension of what the Morodins were trying to do or even the fact that they were sentient. They thought the Morodins were just animals trampling their crops. Eventually, Tropis theorized that the slime trails laid down by the Morodins were vital to the soil's fertility and gave the Morodins free run of several fields. The resulting crop was yellow and inedible; following this, the colonists began to actively chase the Morodins from their fields and [[Hunting/Legends|hunt]] them.<ref name="FC" />

[[File:Karrde-Morodin.jpg|thumb|right|Talon Karrde and Falmal encounter a Morodin in Varonat's Great Jungle.]]
Around [[7 ABY/Legends|7 ABY]], the Morodins encountered a group of [[Krish (species)/Legends|Krish]] who ventured into the Great Jungle planting [[Yagaran aleudrupe plant]]s. Believing the Krish were interested in agricultural cooperation, the Morodins added the newcomers' plantings to their fertilization rounds. Unknown to the Morodins, their nutrient slime chemically changed the pips of the aleudrupe plant's [[Aleudrupe berry/Legends|berries]] which, when combined with [[rethan-K]] and [[promhassic triaxli]], created a [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] formulation as powerful as spin-sealed [[Tibanna/Legends|Tibanna]] gas. The Krish were pleased with the resulting crop, and continued to plant and harvest in the jungle. The Morodins continued to help the newcomers. Every few [[Standard month/Legends|months]], several Morodins were [[Death/Legends|killed]] by hunters in the jungle; to cover their operations, the Krish established a [[Gamgalon's Morodin-hunting safari|safari]] to hunt the Morodins. The leader of the Krish, [[Gamgalon]], discovered that the Morodins were sentient, but established the hunt anyway while paying the local [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Unidentified Imperial governor (Ison Corridor)|governor]] a large bribe to look the other way, as hunting sentient species was prohibited by Imperial law. The Morodins never equated the two groups, the farmers and the hunters, to be from the same source.<ref name="FC" />

[[8 ABY/Legends|A year]] later, the [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Talon Karrde]] and his associate, [[Quelev Tapper]], traveled to Varonat to investigate Gamgalon's operation and see if it was a venture in which they could invest. During the course of their investigation, Karrde and Tapper joined a Morodin-hunting safari, but Karrde could not bring himself to kill a Morodin when he was confronted with one in the jungle as he sensed something was amiss. Later, he and Tapper witnessed a Morodin maze&ndash;running, and deduced that the large creatures were sentient beings. The two smugglers were discovered by Gamgalon, who did not take kindly to outsiders attempting to interfere with his operation. Tapper was killed by the Krish, but Karrde was rescued by a [[Gender/Legends|woman]] called [[Mara Jade Skywalker|Mara Jade]].<ref name="FC" /> Karrde's actions left Gamgalon's operation in ruins.<ref name="GG-Hoth">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20040325web|text=Galactic Gazetteer: Hoth and the Greater Javin|int=Galactic Gazetteer: Hoth and the Greater Javin}}</ref>

{{RPGseed}}
After the discovery of the Morodins' sentience by the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], a team was dispatched to Varonat to make formal contact with them and learn the Morodins' biochemical agriculture. The team had to learn how to communicate with the Morodins, and to study the unique properties of the biochemical slime and deduce how it interacted with the native plant life. The team was also forced to deal with hunters who believed the Morodins were worth more as trophies, and had to contend with the inquisitive Imperial [[Governor/Legends|governor]].<ref name="FC" />
{{Endgame}}

==Morodin in the galaxy==
Morodins were only known to inhabit Varonat, a world on the [[Ison Trade Corridor/Legends|Ison Corridor]]<ref name="FC" /> in the [[Anoat sector/Legends|Anoat sector]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]],<ref name="TEA-OC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}}</ref> during the early years of the New Republic, and their population numbered 50,000 individuals. The location of their original homeworld was unknown to [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] at large as Morodins had been encountered on no other planets as of 8 ABY.<ref name="FC" /> Once the Morodin's sentience became known, it was generally believed that they had either lost or abandoned their advanced organic starship building technology over the millennia.<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The Morodin first appeared in ''[[First Contact]]'', a short story written by [[Timothy Zahn]] for [[West End Games]]' [[Star Wars Adventure Journal 1|''Star Wars Adventure Journal'' 1]] published in [[1994]]. ''First Contact'' was later reprinted in ''[[The Best of the Star Wars Adventure Journal, Issues 1-4]]'' in [[1996]], ''[[Tales from the Empire]]'' in [[1997]], and on [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|''Hyperspace'']]. As the latter two only reprinted the story, the [[Roleplaying game|RPG]] information that included the Morodin's history was not included.

Morodins were later referenced in [[1995]]'s ''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]'' in Mara Jade and Talon Karrde's entries, and in [[1998]]'s ''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' in the Varonat entry. 1998's ''[[Alien Encounters]]'' reprinted the roleplaying lore and statistics from the original ''[[Star Wars Adventure Journal]]'' publication and classified the Morodins as a mammalian species. In [[2004]], Morodins were mentioned in Varonat's entry in ''[[Galactic Gazetteer: Hoth and the Greater Javin]]'' by [[Wizards of the Coast]], and an entry in [[2008]]'s ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''. In [[2009]], the Morodin were mentioned, again in relation to Varonat, in ''[[The Essential Atlas]]''.

The illustration of the Morodin accompanying ''First Contact'' was provided by [[Mike Vilardi]]. For ''Alien Encounters'', the artist who provided the image was not credited specifically for the work as several artists were listed en masse as providing interior art on the table of contents page.
